title: A coherent retraction gives the walking-idempotent colimit
statement: Use the universes, simplicial nerves, quasicategories, coherent functors, homotopies and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $R$ be the small ordinary category with objects $X,Y$, morphism sets $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,X)=\{1_X,e\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)=\{r\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,X)=\{s\}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,Y)=\{1_Y\}$, and composition determined by $r\circ s=1_Y$, $s\circ r=e$, $e^2=e$, $r\circ e=r$ and $e\circ s=s$, together with the identity laws. Write $I=N(R|_{\{X\}})$ for the nerve of the full subcategory with object $X$, and let $j:I\to N(R)$ be the inclusion. For any quasicategory $\mathcal E$ and any coherent functor $F:N(R)\to\mathcal E$, put $H=F\circ j$. The ordinary natural transformation $R|_{\{X\}}\to R$ from the inclusion to the constant functor at $Y$, with component $r$ (its naturality is $r\circ e=r$), induces a coherent cocone $\lambda_F:H\to\Delta_I F(Y)$ after applying nerves and $F$. This cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal E$. Equivalently, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, composition with $\lambda_F$ gives an equivalence of spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(Y),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_I z)$. No other colimits in $\mathcal E$ are assumed.

source.place: HTT Definition 4.4.5.2 and Proposition 4.4.5.12 with its proof, printed pp.304,307 (PDF pp.321,324); I is Idem and N(R) is Idem+. The slice over Y identifies with N(R) and its I-restriction with I, giving precisely the displayed colimit cocone. Corollary 4.4.5.14 records effectivity. Read online; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $A=R|_{\{X\}}$ and let $v:A\to R$ be the ordinary inclusion, so $j=N(v)$. Also let $w:\mathbf1\to R$ send the unique object to $Y$, and write $k=N(w):\Delta^0\to N(R)$. The ordinary transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}_R\to\mathrm{const}_Y$ with components $\eta_X=r$ and $\eta_Y=1_Y$ is natural: for $e$ its equation is $re=r$, for $r$ it is $1_Yr=r$, and for $s$ it is $rs=1_Y$. The identity arrows give the remaining equations. Its nerve is a map $N(R)\times\Delta^1\to N(R)$, since in degree $n$ a functor $[n]\to R\times[1]$ is exactly a pair of functors to the two factors. Postcomposition with $F$ defines a coherent cocone $\mu:F\to\Delta_{N(R)}F(Y)$. Its restrictions are $\mu j=\lambda_F$ and $\mu k=1_{F(Y)}$, including all higher simplices, because the two restricted ordinary transformations are respectively the component-$r$ transformation in the statement and the identity transformation.

source.place: Definition 4.4.5.2; Proposition 4.4.5.12, explicit form of the cocone

proof.text: Compute the ordinary comma categories using the convention that a morphism from $a:b\to X$ to $a':b\to X$ is $h:X\to X$ with $ha=a'$. In $(X\downarrow v)$ the objects are $a=1_X$ and $b=e$; their hom sets are $\operatorname{Hom}(a,a)=\{1_X\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}(a,b)=\{e\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}(b,a)=\varnothing$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(b,b)=\{1_X,e\}$. In $(Y\downarrow v)$ there is just the object $s$, with endomorphisms $1_X,e$, since $es=s$. For $w$, the category $(X\downarrow w)$ has the single object $r$ and its identity; $(Y\downarrow w)$ has the single object $1_Y$ and its identity. Thus the latter two nerves are exactly $\Delta^0$. These calculations use only the displayed composition table of $R$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.11, the two comma categories; terminal-object case used to expand Proposition 4.4.5.12

proof.text: Both comma nerves for $v$ are weakly contractible by explicit simplicial contractions. For $B=(X\downarrow v)$, the arrows $1_X:a\to a$ and $e:a\to b$ give a natural transformation $\mathrm{const}_a\to\mathrm{id}_B$: naturality for the arrow $a\to b$ is $e1_X=e$, and for each endomorphism $h\in\{1_X,e\}$ of $b$ it is $he=e$. For $B=(Y\downarrow v)$, the component $e:s\to s$ gives a transformation $\mathrm{id}_B\to\mathrm{const}_s$, since $e1_X=e$ and $ee=e$. Each transformation is a functor $B\times[1]\to B$, so taking its nerve gives a simplicial homotopy between the identity and the constant map at the indicated object, by the degreewise product identity from step 1. Let $p:N(B)\to\Delta^0$ and let $q$ select that object. Then $pq=1_{\Delta^0}$ and $qp$ is simplicially homotopic to $1_{N(B)}$. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to $p,q$, using the constant homotopy on $\Delta^0$. Hence $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; no Kan hypothesis on these nerves is needed.

source.place: Lemmas 4.4.5.9-4.4.5.11; explicit contraction replacing the cone-retract proof of Lemma 4.4.5.10

proof.text: All ordinary categories just used are small. Apply the ordinary-nerve clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test]: for both $j=N(v)$ and $k=N(w)$ their coherent comma quasicategories are weakly contractible, by steps 2-3. The target $N(R)$ has exactly the two vertices $X,Y$, so these are all the required tests. The coherent comma criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] therefore applies to both inclusions. In particular, for either inclusion any given cocone on an $N(R)$-diagram is colimiting if and only if its restriction is colimiting. The containing universe may be enlarged to contain $\mathcal E$ and both functor categories; the indexing nerves remain small. Neither application requires any colimits to exist in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.11 and Theorem 4.1.3.1; Proposition 4.1.1.8, restriction of a prescribed cocone

proof.text: For the point-indexed diagram with value $F(Y)$, the identity cocone is colimiting. Indeed $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal E)=\mathcal E$ degree by degree, so the map on cocones with any fixed vertex $z$ is composition with $1_{F(Y)}$ on $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(Y),z)$. By the unital assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] this map is simplicially homotopic to the identity. It is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], taking the proposed inverse to be the identity. The mapping-space criterion for cocones, the dual assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], now makes this identity cocone colimiting in the coherent comma sense of the statement.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.12, expansion of the terminal-vertex colimit assertion; mapping-space cocone criterion

proof.text: The cocone $\mu$ of step 1 restricts along $k$ to exactly the identity cocone of step 5. Apply the reflection direction of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] for $k$, whose comma hypothesis was checked in step 4. This proves that this particular $\mu$, with its specified component $r$ at $X$, is a colimiting cocone on $F$. Apply the preservation direction of the same theorem for $j$. Its restriction $\mu j=\lambda_F$ is therefore colimiting, with vertex $F(Y)$. This proves the assertion for the stated cocone rather than only the existence of some cocone with that vertex.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.12, cofinal restriction from the final-vertex cocone, with its last assertion expanded

proof.text: Apply the dual mapping-space criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to $\lambda_F$. For each $z\in\mathcal E$ it gives exactly the equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(Y),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_I z)$ induced by composition with $\lambda_F$. Conversely that criterion identifies this condition with being colimiting in the coherent cocone category. Every cocone used above was constructed explicitly from $F$ or was the identity cocone on one object; no other colimits in $\mathcal E$ have been assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.12; mapping-space formulation of its colimit cocone
